relies on; only the nested Seatbelt fails.

**How to apply:**
- `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is absent from the session's Bash environment,
  but `~/.local/secret/claude-setup-token` is readable from the sandbox:
  a launcher script reads it with `$(<file)`, exports it (never prints it),
  sets `CLAUDE_NESTED=1` and `_CLAUDE_NOTIFY_QUIET=1`, and runs
  `claude --plugin-dir <abs plugin> --print ... --output-format stream-json
  --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools ...`. The pattern is
  `docs/dev/tmp/specflow/hosts/claude-start-insession.bash` +
  `capture-claude.py` in the 00008 worktree; the init event of the stream
  holds `claude_code_version`, `model`, `plugins[]` (source `<name>@inline`
  for `--plugin-dir`) and `skills[]` (`specflow:spec-workflow`). A 50-turn
  skill run cost about 3 USD; a one-word `-p` probe about 0.7 USD.
- Codex's own sandbox cannot apply inside the session Seatbelt: under
  `--sandbox read-only` or `workspace-write` every shell command exits 71
  with the same `sandbox_apply` error (probe it with `echo`). For a scratch
  workspace run `codex-run.sh -y` (bypasses Codex's sandbox; the session
  Seatbelt still confines it), forbid writes in the prompt, and prove it
  with `shasum -a 256` of every workspace file before and after. The
  `CODEX_SESSION_ID` recursion guard only fires inside a Codex session.
- Codex plugin installs need no model session: `codex plugin marketplace add
  <checkout|owner/repo --ref x> --json` then `codex plugin add
  specflow@buvis-agent-plugins --json` in a fresh empty `CODEX_HOME`; Codex
  reads `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` as written and copies the plugin to
  `$CODEX_HOME/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`.
- Claude Code marketplace check in the developer's own profile: `claude
  plugin marketplace add <checkout> --json`, `claude plugin install
  specflow@buvis-agent-plugins --json`, `claude plugin details <id>`,
  then `claude plugin uninstall <id> --json` and `claude plugin marketplace
  remove <name>`; a folder marketplace reads the plugin in place (`plugin
  list` says "Read from: <checkout>/plugins/specflow") and also writes
  `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/...`. `claude plugin validate
  --strict .` validates the root marketplace and advises a README install
  line (`/plugin install specflow --marketplace <owner>/<repo>`).
- `gh pr create --base master --head <branch> --body-file <f>` works with
  the agent PAT; the Validate job finishes in about 30 s.
- Kiro IDE's GitHub import (Powers panel, Add Custom Power, Import power
  from GitHub, repository URL) has no headless form: it stays a developer
  hand-off. See [[review-work-completion-recipe]] for the review side.

Standalone review cycles of spec 00004 (cycles 1-11, 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14) ran with no autopilot state and no `prds/wip/`: the target is `docs/dev/project-management/specs/<spec>/requirements.md`, the design doc is `design.md` beside it, and tasks come from a hand-written `docs/dev/tmp/review-tasks-<id>.json` (copy the previous cycle's; all ten are completed since cycle 6).

**How to apply:**
- Stage with `python3 ~/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/<ver>/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py review-stage --cycle-id 00004c<N> --repo-root <repo> --tasks-json ... --prd ... --design-doc ... --roster alice,blake,bob,carl --since <prior head_sha> --replay-cmd "python3 -m pytest" --prior-findings ... --settled-ledger docs/dev/project-management/reviews/00004-artifact-state-contract-ledger.json --gate-command "sh <repo>/docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/gate.sh"`. It finishes in about 10 s.
- Reusable tooling is saved in `docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/` (untracked): `gate.sh` runs the five CI steps from `.github/workflows/validate.yml` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, one log each under `gate-logs/`; `build_bob_retry.py <cycle> <base> <head>` builds Bob's inlined retry prompt from the staged files and those logs. `review-stage` cannot parse unittest counts, so compose the `Tests:` line from the `Ran N tests` lines (cycle 11 review: 12 + 52 + 304 = 368; after its rework the contract suite is 308).
- The spec has no frontmatter, so `consensus_engine` is `legacy` and `doubt_reviewer` is `codex`; Eve stays disabled (no state file, no codex-implemented task record).
- The Agent tool in this build has no `run_in_background` parameter; subagents run in the background by default. Dispatch Alice and Blake as `autopilot:alice` / `autopilot:blake` with `effort: high`, with a prompt that tells them to Read their rendered prompt file and follow it. Bob and Carl are background Bash. No Watcher (interactive session).
- Bob's resumed-thread run refuses for lack of input every cycle (cycles 2-11; codex sandbox blocks reads: `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`; in 00006 cycle 1 the aegis Fact-Forcing Gate hook blocked his `cat` instead, same remedy). The inlined retry was 773 KB for 00006 (560 KB diff) and codex handled it in a few minutes. In cycle 11 the refusal was prose only, with no `[BOB] ⚪ Cannot statically verify` line, so the three-pattern rule did not match literally; treat it as the refusal (it is also the malformed-output trigger) and dispatch the pre-built inlined retry without `--resume-thread`. Copy the first output to `bob-output-<id>-first.txt` before the retry overwrites it. The retry overwrites `bob-thread-<id>.txt` with its own thread; stamp that one. His `[BOB]` lines were unbulleted in cycles 10-11; strip a `- ` bullet into a `-lines.txt` copy only when present.
- Carl failed cycles 2-8 with copilot "Authentication failed" (exit 1); cycles 9-11 ran fine (exit 0, `gemini-3.8-flash`). Always dispatch him; on failure, one unchanged retry per policy, then record unavailable; nothing to latch standalone. His `-o` file includes copilot's tool transcript before the `[CARL]` line; the consolidator copes. In cycle 11 his shell ran the suite without `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, then `find . -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +` in the repo: check `git status --ignored=matching plugins tools tests` afterwards (00005 and 00006 left `__pycache__` under `tests/` and `tools/`; `git clean -X -d -f -- plugins tools tests` removes only those).
- The engram pack fails with a readonly sqlite DB every cycle (in a worktree: "not inside a registered repo"); degraded, not blocking.
- From 00005 on (2026-10-16), work happens in per-spec worktrees under `~/git/src/worktrees/agent-plugins/feature-specflow-<spec>`. `review-tools/` hardcodes the main checkout, so copy `gate.sh` and `build_bob_retry.py` into the worktree's `docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/` with the worktree path; CI has 7 steps since 00005 (adds `tests/specflow/rules` and `check_rules.py --area ...`, nine areas since 00006). The 00006 worktree already holds seven-step copies. A standalone cycle 1 in a worktree passes `--since <merge-base with master>`; the whole staging took 8 s and the four reviewers about 25 min (Carl last). `rg` skips gitignored `docs/dev/tmp/` unless `--no-ignore`. aegis blocks shell redirects into `docs/dev/tmp/`: send Carl's stderr to the scratchpad. Commit messages: aegis blocks `Co-Authored-By` trailers.
- The pytest fail-first replay reports `subTest` failures as passes. Always do the unittest replay by hand: a detached worktree at the base sha, copy HEAD's tests in with `cp -R src/. dst/`, run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/specflow/contract -t tests/specflow/contract -k <name> -k <name>...` with bytecode off. The same worktree moved to HEAD (`git checkout -f --detach <head>`) serves mutation runs; remove it with `git worktree remove --force`.
- `consolidate_findings.py` merges findings on the same file too eagerly: the "two shared all-digit tokens" rule fires on requirement IDs like `VAL-001.8` (ledger mis-dismissals, cycle 10), and "matched only after suffix stripping" merged two different `checks.py` defects at `:507` and `:528` into one row (cycle 11). Read the merge warning line and the Auto-dismissed block every cycle and split or restore by hand.
- CI pins Python 3.10 while local `python3` is 3.14: OS-error edge cases differ (`Path.exists()` raises `PermissionError` on 3.10, returns False on 3.14). Probe with `uv run --no-project --python 3.10 python -I <script>`; the contract suite under 3.10 takes 4 s.
- A ledger entry whose reason is time-bound ("trial open") keeps dismissing after the fact changes: cycle 6 restored Blake's Kiro-link finding after T-027 closed. Prune or update such entries when their condition ends.
- A direct test run writes `plugins/specflow/skills/spec-workflow/scripts/__pycache__`, which then fails `test_script_runs_from_any_python_start_and_leaves_no_bytecode` and `verify_release.py`. Keep `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (or `python3 -B` for probes that import the helper). `verify_release.py` also refuses modified tracked package files: commit the fix first, then re-run it.
- Blake's F23 re-raises (placeholder and bugfix checks, deferred to 00005/00006) and the cycle-10 F10 scans are absorbed by the ledger every cycle; the script prints the placeholder entry's reason for the bugfix line. The consolidator only dismisses a blind reviewer's ledger re-raises when told so: `consolidate_findings.py --ledger <ledger> --ledger-dismiss blake alice:<f> blake:<f> bob:<f> carl:<f>` (00006 cycle 2: three of Blake's rows dismissed, each with the ledger reason).
- `check_review_file.py` takes `--review-file <path> --require-codex-guard` (a bare path is a usage error). `--prior-findings` is inlined verbatim under "### Prior cycle findings", so write `docs/dev/tmp/review-prior-findings-<id>.md` as the prior table with a Disposition column (fixed, accepted, ledger) and the rework commits named; reviewers then verify fixes instead of re-raising rows.
- A cycle-1 🟠 that gets fixed means an incremental cycle 2: `--since <cycle-1 head_sha>` (the diff then covers the review-doc, decisions, fix and outcome commits), `--prior-findings`, `--settled-ledger`, and Bob with `--resume-thread <cycle-1 thread>`, which refused for lack of input again (00006 cycle 2); the inlined retry for a 200 KB diff was 201 KB and took about four minutes. Cycle 2 staged in 6 s; the reviewers took 5 min (Alice, Bob retry, Carl) to 10 min (Blake). The lead may downgrade a reviewer's 🟠 with evidence (00006 cycle 2, F2 and F3), but ask the developer whether the downgrades stand before calling the cycle converged.
- The pytest replay flags a coverage test of a branch that already existed (00006 F9's eight tests) as "passes at base": a fact, not a defect.

**Rework after the walkthrough (cycle-10 and cycle-11 pattern):** one `docs(specflow): record the 00004 cycle-N walkthrough decisions` commit (minutes appended to the review file, ledger entries), then `fix(specflow): apply the 00004 cycle-N review decisions` (code, tests, CHANGELOG line under `### Fixed`, which is the last section), then `docs(specflow): record the 00004 cycle-N outcome`. A `design.md` edit adds a qa-log entry and a re-approval question; a module move that the design's placement text already covers needs none.
- Write the tests first and run them with `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests/specflow/contract -t tests/specflow/contract -k <name>` for the fail-first evidence; a guard test that passes at base by design gets mutation evidence in a worktree at the fix commit instead.
- Editing a helper module trips two hooks: the Fact-Forcing Gate on the first Edit per file (present in the message the importers from `rg -n "from \.module import|from specflow_helper\.module import"`, the affected public functions, and the data shapes, then retry) and Echo, which reads a moved function as a duplicate (the retry passes).
- A finding that needs code moved out of a file the approved design places it in (00005 F2/F3, 800-line limit) means a design edit: ask the developer first (design edit + re-approval vs accept), edit `## Module placement` and the tree, add a qa-log "Review NNNNN-01 design edits" entry, fix, then ask the re-approval with blobs and canonical hashes from `hash --json`, write `.specflow.json` (fresh `code-baseline` over the placement paths), and `reconcile`. After the fix, re-read the placement rows against the real diff before recording the approval: in 00005 `checks.py` ended byte-identical to base, so its "edit" row was false and `__init__.py` was missing, which cost a second approval question. To register checks from a new module without a bottom-of-file import (E402 plus aegis's ban on `noqa`), import it from `specflow_helper/__init__.py`.
- `uvx` cannot write `~/.local/share/uv/tools` under the sandbox; run ruff as `uv run --no-project --with ruff ruff check <files>` and `... ruff format --check <files>`. Four findings are pre-existing (`spec_text.py` SIM102 in `sources_value`, `test_checks.py` ISC004 x3).
- Re-approval mechanics (00006, 2026-10-18): `validate_spec.py hash <spec>/design.md --json` and `... tasks.md --json` give `sha256`, `approvedAt`, `approvedCommit`, `upstreamSha256`; `code-baseline <spec> --paths <repo-relative paths...>` prints `approvedCode` for the placement files (19 for 00006). Ask the developer with the blobs (`git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`) and canonical hashes, write `.specflow.json` with the Write tool from those values, then `reconcile` and `status --json` (warnings drop to none with the fresh baseline). A design-text-only edit needs no code change; the qa-log lives in `docs/dev/project-management/intake/processed/specflow/<spec>/qa-log.md`.
- The Fact-Forcing Gate blocks the first Edit of every file in a session, JSON evals and sessions included; it accepts the facts written in the message text (importers via `rg`, affected names, data shape) and the retry passes. The 00005 completion ticks pattern held for 00006's four boxes: `status` reports `complete` once all are ticked.
- 00007 build (2026-10-18/19), PR #6, worktree `feature-specflow-00007`: its `review-tools/` copies have eight gate steps (adds `tests/specflow/review`) and the area list through `CNV`; `build_bob_retry.py` reads `review.log` too. `verify_release.py` forbids the literal `tests/specflow` inside any package file, even in a rule-tag comment (reword the tag). The `placeholders` check reads `Outcome:` lines in `tasks.md`, so never write the forbidden placeholder words there, even to say they were searched for. `check_rules.py` with no `--area` passes since T-080. Echo also flags a helper name repeated across scratchpad generator scripts; the retry passes.
- 00007 cycle 1 (2026-10-19, review `960f303`): uncommitted `ruff format` output in seven session fixtures made `review-stage` skip the gate as dirty; a tagged `git stash push -m ... -- <paths>`, restage, `stash apply <sha>` + drop afterwards fixed it. Bob ran clean on the first inlined dispatch (no refusal). Carl's first run exited 0 with only a tool transcript (no `[CARL]` line, no verdicts): format-invalid, and one retry with the format correction appended to a copy of his prompt returned a proper all-clear. The pytest replay again listed a `subTest` test as passing at base; unittest showed it erroring.
- 00007 rework (2026-10-25, decisions `7ff65ed`, fixes `0783028`..`3ed1576`): the lead adjudicated the 18 findings alone under the standing authorization (no walkthrough with the developer), merged `master` first (PR 5's fix had taken SR-VAL-019..025, colliding with T-079's two rules; placement-drift folded into SR-VAL-020 with both sources, design-sections renumbered SR-VAL-026, the T-079 Outcome reworded; Outcome lines are not hashed, `stale` stayed empty), then ran four sub-agents in the one worktree on disjoint file allowlists (check_links: opus high; receipt check: sonnet medium; the High F3 bugfix branch: opus high; rule text: opus medium), each told not to commit, and committed each cluster itself after reading the diff, with the CHANGELOG `### Fixed` line added by the lead at commit time. Two agents appending to `inventory.json` in different areas was fine; `git apply --cached` of a hand-cut hunk staged one agent's rows without the other's. A merge commit subject is not conventional, so the aegis hook needs `git commit -F <file>`. Two lessons: after a validator check changes, run `validate_spec.py status` on THIS repository's own specs before committing (the first F1 regex rejected every real receipt, since each ends `COMPLETE (…).`, and closed 00007's implementation gate); and an agent that narrows a rule should be told to sweep the same file for sibling rules that restate the old reading (SR-RVD-025 repeated SR-RVD-006's).

Carl failed on copilot "exceeded your monthly quota" (exit 1, twice): recorded unavailable, the native gemini backend not tried (other billing). Blake 2 min, Alice 2 min. name: design-solution
description: Use when turning a PRD into a reviewed design doc (the HOW) before planning tasks - architecture fit, exact interfaces, reuse, alternatives, then an autonomous adversarial review. Triggers on "design solution", "design this PRD".
argument-hint: "<prd-path> [--rework <review-file>]"
---

# Design Solution

Turn a PRD (the WHAT) into a reviewed implementation design doc (the HOW): module
placement, exact interfaces, data flow, reuse of existing code, and alternatives
weighed - then critique the draft with an autonomous adversarial reviewer before
handing it to `/autopilot:plan-tasks`.

This skill runs **unattended** inside the autopilot build gate. It never asks the
user anything. It is **state-agnostic**: it prints the design doc path on success
and, when unresolved cardinal sins or blockers remain, ends with an explicit
FAILED report naming them (a model-followed skill has no exit code - the report
is the observable signal the caller checks); the caller records the path.

It **never edits the PRD**. The design refines the PRD; acceptance criteria stay
PRD-owned.

## Dependencies

- Own files: `references/cardinal-sins.md` (the severity taxonomy, inlined into
  every reviewer prompt). It ships with this pack; `review-design-doc` keeps its
  own copy for its own use, so edit the two together when the taxonomy changes.
- Pack skills (files read at runtime): `use-codex` (`scripts/codex-run.sh`)
- CLI: `codex` (review dispatch). Unavailable: fall back to the Claude subagent
  reviewer documented in the review step
- Optional: `~/.claude/rules-library/rationalizations.md` (host-local; supplies
  the synonym sets for the reuse sweep). Absent: run the sweep with your own
  verb/noun synonyms and say so in the sweep's summary line.
- Optional: cartographer atlas `~/.local/share/agents/cartographer/projects/<hash>/atlas.md`
  (skipped silently when absent)

## Inputs

- **PRD path** (argument). If omitted, auto-select the single PRD in
  `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`. Error and stop if `wip/` holds zero or 2+ PRDs
  ("ambiguous - pass the PRD path explicitly").
- **Rework mode** (`--rework <review-file>`): design one review cycle's
  CRITICAL fixes instead of the PRD's first implementation - see
  `## Rework mode`.
- **Architecture context**, loaded when present (skip silently if absent):
  - the cartographer atlas for this repo
    (`~/.local/share/agents/cartographer/projects/<hash>/atlas.md`)
  - `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`
  - `AGENTS.md` / `agent_docs/`

## Output

`docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md`, where `<prd-stem>` is the PRD filename
minus its `.md` extension. Create `docs/dev/project-management/designs/` if missing - it is a
durable artifact dir, like `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/`.

In rework mode the output is `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-rework-<cycle>-design.md`,
where `<cycle>` is the review file's `review:` frontmatter value.

## Rework mode

`/autopilot:design-solution <prd-path> --rework <review-file>` designs one
review cycle's CRITICAL fixes (PRD 00194). `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6
invokes it once per cycle, before any fix task is created. Steps 1-5 run as
in default mode except where a bullet below says otherwise.

- **Inputs** (step 1): the PRD, plus from `<review-file>`: `<cycle>` = its
  `review:` frontmatter value, and the CRITICAL rows = every
  `## Consolidated Findings` table row whose Severity cell is `🔴 Critical`.
  `<work_start_sha>` = the left side of the `Diff range:` line in the cycle-1
  review file beside it, `<prd-stem>-review-1.md` (or `-review-01.md`) - under
  autopilot that range is `work_start_sha..HEAD`, so no flag carries it. Run
  `git diff --stat <work_start_sha>..HEAD` for the PRD's whole work range, and
  on cycle 2 or later also `git diff --stat` over `<review-file>`'s own
  `Diff range:` (the prior cycle's rework commits, the range the prior fix
  changed); a `Diff range:` holding a single SHA `X` is read as
  `X..<head_sha>`, `<head_sha>` being `<review-file>`'s frontmatter value. A
  review file with no `🔴 Critical` row, or no cycle-1 review file with a
  `Diff range:` line, is a usage error: print
  `design-solution: --rework needs a 🔴 Critical row and a cycle-1 Diff range` and
  stop without writing a doc.
- **Output**: `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-rework-<cycle>-design.md` with the
  same nine sections, same headings, same order as step 3, preceded by one
  source line directly under the H1 title, exactly
  `Source review: <review-file> (head_sha <head_sha>)` - the review file path
  as given and its frontmatter `head_sha`. Phase 6 compares that line before
  reusing a doc, so a design reviewed for one cycle's findings never supplies
  the contract for another's. An existing file at that path is overwritten.
- **`## Architecture fit` opens with a `Prior fix:` paragraph** -
  what the prior fix changed and why it regressed, quoting the CRITICAL rows'
  evidence and the files the prior-cycle `git diff --stat` names, and saying
  whether each CRITICAL was introduced by that fix or only exposed by it. On
  cycle 1 it reads exactly `Prior fix: none - there was no prior rework fix.`
- **`## Interfaces & contracts` is the sole contract source** for the cycle's
  CRITICAL fix tasks: Phase 6 copies it verbatim into each CRITICAL
  `[D{cycle}]` task's `### Contract` block, so name every symbol exactly, and
  open each entry with the 🔴 row it closes (`Closes: <row text>`) so a task
  owner is readable from the shared block.
- **Review** (step 4): the same three-dispatch procedure, the same 3-dispatch ceiling,
  prompt package, minimum-engagement check and Claude fallback, unchanged. The
  prompt additionally carries the CRITICAL rows verbatim so a reviewer judges
  the fix design against the finding it must close.
- **Terminal result line** (step 5): after the exit report is decided, append
  its `result:` value as the last line of `## Review log`, unindented - exactly
  `result: ok` or `result: failed (open cardinal sins/blockers)`. The Review log
  is the ninth section, so this is the doc's last non-empty line; Phase 6 reads
  it as the pass gate. Default mode writes no such line.
- **Exit report**: the first line is `design-solution: <prd-stem> (rework cycle <n>)`
  and `doc:` names the rework path; the remaining lines are unchanged. Open
  cardinal sins or blockers after dispatch 3 end the report with
  `result: failed (open cardinal sins/blockers)` exactly as step 5 describes;
  the caller routes the failure.

### 2. Reuse sweep (before designing any new code)

Search the codebase (Bash `rg`; the native Grep tool is absent in this build,
see rules/tools.md) for existing helpers and patterns that already do what the PRD

- Search **both** the verb and the noun synonyms (e.g. `format` / `render` /
  `serialize` AND `date` / `timestamp`).
- If a search returns nothing, re-run it with a term you know is present to prove

Record findings in `## Reuse inventory`: one entry per existing helper as
**(path + how to use it)**, or, when nothing exists, an explicit

### 3. Write the design doc

sections, these headings, in this order**:

1. `## Architecture fit` - the target layers/modules this work lands in, drawn

2. `## Module placement` - which changes are new files vs edits to existing

name: use-sonnet
description: Use when running Anthropic Claude Sonnet via the native claude CLI (headless) for code analysis, refactoring, or editing. Triggers on "run sonnet", "sonnet analyze", "ask sonnet".
compatibility: "Portable standalone compatibility copy of the autopilot plugin skill; it ships its own helper script and needs the named model CLI on PATH. Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill."
---

> **Paths in this pack.** The helper this skill runs ships here, under
> `~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/`. A path written as
> `<autopilot-plugin-root>/...` is the exception: it lives in the autopilot
> plugin, which ships the rest of the pack, and that step is unavailable without
> it. Substitute the plugin's root yourself; never pass the literal marker to a
> shell.

# Sonnet Skill Guide

Sonnet is accessed via the native `claude` CLI (headless `-p`). The helper script defaults to the `sonnet` alias (latest base Sonnet) and exposes `-m/--model` for explicit overrides. This uses your Claude quota, not Copilot credits - never route Sonnet (or any model Claude already provides) through `copilot`.

## Dependencies

- Files read from other skill dirs:
  `~/.agents/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md` - mandatory,
  applies verbatim (see below)
  - `<autopilot-plugin-root>/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/detect_usage_limit.py` - optional,
    for a deterministic reset-epoch parse of a usage-limit banner (see
    "Usage-limit banner" below)
- CLIs: `claude` (native, headless `-p`); `mise` for resolution

## Dispatch Contract (shared)

Background dispatch and waiting (TaskOutput-only waiting), following up, error handling, and the always-use-`-f` prompt rule are defined once in `~/.agents/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md`. Read it before dispatching; it applies verbatim to this skill.

## Usage-limit banner (claude backend only)

`claude -p` is the one backend that can hit the **Claude usage limit** mid-run: instead of a normal result it returns a banner like `You've hit your session limit · resets 8:10pm (Europe/Prague)` (also `weekly`/`usage` limit; a stream-json run additionally carries a rejected `rate_limit_event` with a machine-readable `resetsAt` epoch). This is neither a task failure nor retryable — the quota is spent until the reset.

**Detect** it by scanning the run's output / `-o` file for the same markers `detect_usage_limit.py` uses: `hit your (session|usage|weekly) limit` or `usage limit reached`, and `resets <HH[:MM]> <am|pm> (<tz>)` for the reset time. For a deterministic reset epoch, run `python3 <autopilot-plugin-root>/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/detect_usage_limit.py --log <the -o output file>` — exit 0 prints the reset epoch (it parses both the prose banner and a stream-json `resetsAt`); exit 1 means no live limit.

**On a hit:** mark the run **FAILED**, report the reset time in the run report (`usage limit; resets <time>`), and do NOT retry before the reset — a retry re-fails identically. Under autopilot the `autoclaude` wrapper already sleeps-until-reset at the loop boundary; a standalone `use-sonnet` run cannot wait, so it stops and surfaces the reset for the user.

## Effort Policy

The wrapper passes `--effort` explicitly in every mode. Defaults follow the
selected model: Haiku/low, Sonnet/medium, Opus/high, Fable/xhigh. Use
`--effort high` for reviews regardless of the selected model. An explicit
`--effort` overrides the tier default; invalid levels fail before launching.
Session and user-global effort settings are not used as wrapper defaults.

## Model Policy

- **Default:** `sonnet` (latest base Sonnet). Use unless the user asks for a different model.
- **`-m/--model` override:** pass a `claude` alias (`opus`, `haiku`) or a full model id (`claude-sonnet-5`). Opus costs more of your Claude quota - confirm with the user before defaulting to it for routine work.

## Running a Task

1. Select the permission mode required for the task; default to no special flags (interactive approval) unless edits are necessary.
2. Assemble the command with appropriate options:
   - `-m, --model MODEL` to override the default (`sonnet`); ask the user first if the override is a costlier tier (e.g. `opus`)
   - `-f, --file FILE` to read the prompt from a file (preferred - avoids shell escaping)
   - `-i, --interactive <prompt>` for interactive mode with initial prompt
   - `-a, --allow-edits` to auto-approve file edits only (maps to `--permission-mode acceptEdits`; Bash and other tools stay gated, so an unattended agentic child can stall on a prompt)
   - `-y, --yolo` for full permissions (`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`); REQUIRED for unattended agentic dispatches that must run commands. Note: a `-y` child runs with no warden or hook filtering
   - `-d, --dir <DIR>` to allow access to specific directories (maps to `--add-dir`)
   - `-s, --silent` accepted for compatibility (claude `-p` output is already clean)
3. When continuing a previous session, use `-c`/`--continue` or `-r`/`--resume [sessionId]`.
4. Run the command, capture output, and summarize the outcome for the user.
5. **After Sonnet completes**, inform the user: "You can resume this session with 'sonnet resume' or 'claude --continue'."

### Quick Reference

| Use case | Key flags |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only analysis | `-f prompt.txt` |
| Interactive with initial prompt | `-i "prompt"` |
| Auto-approve edits only | `-a -f prompt.txt` |
| Full auto, unattended agentic (edits + commands) | `-y -f prompt.txt` |
| Allow specific directory | `-d <DIR> -f prompt.txt` |
| Resume recent session | `--continue` |
| Resume specific session | `--resume [sessionId]` |
| Scripting (clean output) | `-s -f prompt.txt` |

## Helper Script

```bash
# Write prompt to temp file (see the shared dispatch contract), then run
bash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# With auto-approve edits (Bash still gated)
bash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -a -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# Override model (only after user approval - costlier tier)
bash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -m opus -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# Full permissions
bash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -y -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# Resume session
bash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -r

# Capture output to file
bash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -a -o /tmp/result.txt -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt
```

Run `~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh --help` for all options.

FILE docs/dev/project-management/designs/00018-autopilot-controller-kernel-v1-design.md
# Autopilot controller kernel and protocol design

## Architecture fit

AP00018 introduces the sole portable workflow writer under `plugins/autopilot/controller/`. It does not activate legacy skills or certify a host. AP00019 adds lifecycle/jobs, AP00020 review authority, AP00021 records. OVCAQ remains untouched. Extraction source is OVCAQ commit `cf8be72214a515c84ee42f0d8b30e65cc2a4ebb7`, inspected with `git show`, never checkout HEAD. All tests use temporary roots.

## Module placement

New runtime files: `controller/main.py`, `controller/autopilot_state/{__init__,schema,store,paths,protocol,actors}.py`, relative to the plugin root. New bundle files: `contracts/controller/{workflow-v1,fixtures-v1,provenance}.json` and `contracts/controller-v1.json`. New maintainer exporter: `tools/autopilot/export-controller-contract.py`. Tests: `tests/autopilot/test_controller_{kernel,protocol,actors}.py`. Edit `plugins/autopilot/README.md` and `plugins/autopilot/CHANGELOG.md`. Characterization/ownership/source-to-target maps live in `contracts/controller/provenance.json`; fixture inputs and expected outcomes live in `fixtures-v1.json`. No supervisor or launcher imports.

## Interfaces & contracts

### Kernel

Python floor is 3.12; stdlib only. `autopilot_state.schema` exports `SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`, `MAX_STATE_BYTES = 16777216`, `MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 2097152`, `MAX_STRING_BYTES = 1048576`, `MAX_JSON_DEPTH = 32`, `MAX_JSON_INTEGER_DIGITS = 640`, `SchemaError`, `ResourceLimitError`, `decode_json(text: str, *, source: str)`, `validate_state(value: object) -> dict`, and `new_state(*, repo_root: Path, project_id: str, workflow_id: str) -> dict`. Reject duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, bool integers, unknown owned fields and unsupported durable versions; validate before deep copying. Default review cap is 2. Reject process identity, PID, launcher, heartbeat, resource usage and TUI state as workflow fields. Model/session observations later arrive only as explicitly bounded workflow evidence, never execution authority.

Retain source `StateStore(path: Path, *, boundary_hook=None)`, `read()`, `initialize(initial)`, `transaction(mutator, *, expected_revision=None, publication_guard=None)`, `restore(*, expected_revision=None, precondition=None)`, source exception names and six `DurabilityBoundary` values. Preserve source lock/read/publication guards, single-link regular-file checks, bounded reads, CAS under exclusive flock, deep-copy mutation, revision increment, fsync-before-replace, backup/state pair repair and create-only initialization. Keep one last-good `.bak` and `.lock`; failed validation/conflict/publication cannot change the pair. Restore is an offline forensic library primitive, never a CLI operation or a protocol recovery path. It requires readable valid current state and valid backup and refuses with BackupError unless backup lease_epoch, owner, actors and receipts exactly equal current and no credential-intent.json exists. Check these invariants under the same exclusive lock after decoding backup and before any pair publication; precondition(current) alone is insufficient. Only security-identical backups may be restored, with current revision +1. This deliberate tightening of source restore prevents epoch rollback, credential resurrection and receipt loss; characterize it explicitly. Test acquire followed by restore refuses with exact state/backup/credential bytes preserved, and a security-identical backup restore retains source revision and repair outcomes. Corrupt current state refuses with recovery_required and preserves bytes for operator forensic recovery. Never silently overwrite corruption. Test backup/restore and each injected boundary. Unsupported directory fsync refuses explicitly.

`resolve_project_root(path: Path) -> Path` resolves an existing directory without ancestor workflow inference. The private controller store is `<project-root>/.autopilot/controller/`, directory 0700, with `state.json`, `state.json.bak`, `state.json.lock`, and `actors/`. Before creating any credential, create regular private `.gitignore` files containing `*\n` in both `.autopilot/` and the private controller directory (parent 0700, files 0600; sibling archives are ignored too), refuse an existing incompatible or aliased ignore file, and verify a temporary Git repository ignores state and actor files. This is separate from the implementation batch's legacy state. Reject symlink components below the resolved project root, escapes, nonregular/multiply-linked artifacts and payload-selected state paths. Preserve directory descriptor/no-follow creation and ancestor inode identity rechecks from the pinned root resolver; Path.resolve containment alone is insufficient. Project identity is SHA-256 of the resolved root's UTF-8 path. Relocating the installed package preserves functionality; relocating an existing project requires explicit future migration, not identity rewriting.

Durable state has closed top-level keys `schema_version`, `revision`, `project_id`, `workflow_id`, `repo_root`, `lease_epoch`, `owner`, `actors`, `receipts`, `workflow`. `workflow` is exactly `{batch: null, work: null, tasks: [], review: {cap: 2}, recovery: null, jobs: []}` in this kernel; no operation may mutate these reserves. Later producer PRDs define their expanded schemas and migration. Characterization records each source workflow field and its deferred owner; it does not import process fields or claim full legacy schema equivalence. No generic JSON setter is exported. `owner` is null or `{actor_id, mode, native_session_id, lease_epoch}`; `mode` is `manual|supervised`. `actors` contains descriptors, never credential secrets. `receipts` maps request IDs to canonical request digests, actor binding and complete original responses. `jobs` is empty and cannot be mutated in AP00018. Actor registry retains only the current operator and current owner descriptors (at most two); historical authorizing digests are receipt-owned, never actor rows. Normal receipt admission stops at 4094 entries. Before writing durable intent or any final credential, serialize and validate the complete candidate and complete response. Normal operation candidates may occupy at most 14680064 bytes (14 MiB), leaving 2097152 bytes for the two emergency operations below the 16777216-byte state ceiling. Each stored core response is bounded to 65536 UTF-8 bytes, including all absolute paths; refuse a root/response that cannot meet this bound before bootstrap. Emergency release/recover may use the reserved bytes only when clearing an active owner; their complete candidate must still validate under the state ceiling. A no-owner call cannot consume reserve capacity. Maximum response/descriptor growth for both emergency operations fits within 2 MiB under these explicit core bounds; test byte saturation independently of receipt-count saturation and reject oversized candidates before preparing intent. This prepublication check is part of the transaction admission, not a later _canonical_bytes failure after credentials changed. Reserve two further slots exclusively for owner.release/owner.recover; these may clear an active owner at saturation, never acquire a new one. At 4096 entries the workflow is sealed against all new mutations; exact receipt retrieval and snapshot remain available. Capacity is an explicit terminal boundary, not an unspecified future repair. Operator exit procedure: finish/reconcile jobs (none supported here), release/recover ownership using reserve capacity, verify an owner-null snapshot, copy the entire private controller directory to a private offline archive and verify every file hash, then rename the original private directory into a sibling private archive named by workflow ID, and open a new workflow at the fixed empty controller path. Never delete the archive. Archived state, credentials, receipts and schema remain replayable by placing the original directory back at its original project binding while the new workflow is offline; never merge identities. README documents the ordered manual procedure; tests saturate normal capacity, clear the owner through reserved capacity, validate the archive/hash/restore roundtrip and open a distinct workflow. No archival or state removal runs automatically. If an active owner reaches hard capacity through externally corrupted state, return recovery_required and retain all evidence rather than overriding it. Top-level `lease_epoch` starts at 0 and increases on acquire/recover/release, retained even while owner is null.

### Protocol

CLI argv is `["python3", "<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py"]`. Commands are `--json contract`, `--json snapshot --project-root PATH`, `--json apply --project-root PATH --request FILE`; apply accepts `--actor-file PATH`. No shell invocation or process launch. Request file limit is 2097152 bytes; snapshot/response output limit is 16777216 bytes. Use strict bounded JSON parsing. Exit 0 for success, 1 for structured rejection, 2 for argument misuse; never print credentials or untrusted request values in diagnostics. CLI callers must bound execution time; tests use a 30-second subprocess deadline.

Envelope is exactly `{protocol_major, operation, request_id, expected_revision, project_id, workflow_id, actor_id, job_id, lease_epoch, payload}`. `protocol_major` is integer 1; request_id and nonnull identities are nonempty strings of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; expected_revision and nonnull lease_epoch are nonnegative integers, never bool. Operator job_id is null. Response is exactly `{ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable}`; success has error_code null and retryable false; failure has result null. Error codes are exactly `invalid_request`, `incompatible_contract`, `revision_conflict`, `wrong_binding`, `missing_capability`, `rejected_evidence`, `recovery_required`. Only revision_conflict is retryable. Rejections retain current revision, or 0 before initialization. Reject malformed envelopes before touching state. Redact diagnostics.

AP00018 implements `workflow.open`, `owner.acquire`, `owner.release`, `owner.recover` and advertises only `workflow.core.v1`. Closed later names are `policy.bind`, `prd.enter`, `task.replace`, `task.start`, `task.finish`, `task.attempt`, `lane.route`, `job.plan`, `job.claim`, `job.record_exit`, `review.record_stage`, `review.close`, `custody.record`, `custody.discharge`, `verification.record`, `phase.handoff`, `prd.stall`, `prd.park`, `prd.defer`, `prd.complete`, `artifact.record`, `records.commit`; these return missing_capability without writes. Unknown operation returns invalid_request. Jobs/reviews/records/waves capabilities are declared unavailable, never advertised or returned as successful stubs.

Payload schemas are closed objects: workflow.open `{}`; owner.acquire `{mode: "manual"|"supervised", native_session_id: nonempty string}`; owner.release `{}`; owner.recover `{reason: nonempty string, reconciled_job_ids: unique string[]}`. Strings obey the identity bound except reason, bounded to 4096 bytes. Freeze schemas and positive/negative fixtures for all four implemented operations. Reserved operation names and their unavailable capability mappings are explicit contract declarations, not implemented payload schemas.

Fresh workflow.open on an absent store alone accepts null workflow_id/actor_id/lease_epoch, null job_id, expected_revision 0 and matching project_id. Assign workflow ID once, create operator credential, state and receipt recoverably under one bootstrap lock. Result contains `workflow_id`, `actor_id`, `actor_file`, `lease_epoch`; only credential path is returned. Initialize receipt and revision 0 together. Identical fresh-open replay after lost acknowledgement returns that exact result without creating credentials or workflows; conflicting ID returns revision_conflict. Existing workflow.open requires a valid actor and all existing bindings; it cannot reset or acquire ownership.

Other apply calls authenticate actor-file against its stored current descriptor or a receipt-retained historical descriptor before any mutation. Check project/workflow binding, scope and job first. For an identical recorded request, either a credential matching the receipt's historical authorizing digest or the authenticated current credential of that same actor_id and role at an epoch not earlier than the authorizing epoch may retrieve only that receipt even if its epoch was revoked; this never grants mutation authority. For any new request, require current descriptor and exact current envelope/credential epoch, then CAS and operation preconditions, then persist state plus receipt atomically. Current-credential receipt retrieval uses the historical envelope unchanged and does not require its lease_epoch to equal the current epoch. Historical credentials cannot submit new operations, altered envelopes or recover ownership. Thus in-place operator-file rotation does not prevent the caller reopening that path and retrieving its original receipt after lost acknowledgement; a caller retaining the old bytes may also retrieve that receipt only. Same canonical complete envelope (including expected_revision) under an authenticated binding returns the original response even after revision changes; changed request ID payload/envelope conflicts. Historical receipt retrieval is the sole exception to execution-epoch revocation and returns no credential contents; it cannot replay effects into new ownership. Retain each receipt's original authorizing digest and response until explicit future migration; capacity refusal never evicts them. Unsupported operation and rejected requests never create receipts or change revisions. Contract/snapshot do not acquire execution ownership; snapshot excludes all credential material.

### Actors and lease

Credential files are strict JSON with closed keys `{actor_id, project_id, workflow_id, role, lease_epoch, native_session_id, secret}`. Generate secrets using `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, store only SHA-256 digests in durable actor descriptors, compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. Credential root 0700/file 0600; reject symlinks, hardlinks, wrong permissions and bindings. File contents never enter logs, responses, bundle fixtures or public snapshot. Bootstrap operator is role operator at epoch 0. Execution credential role is owner; its scope allows release and future permitted lifecycle actions, never operator recovery. Future job role is declared but no job credential issuance occurs here.

owner.acquire requires current operator authority and no owner; increment epoch, rotate the operator credential to that epoch, and issue one owner credential bound to mode/native_session_id. Operator actor ID remains stable, its new secret replaces the old secret; every epoch-changing operation rotates it in the same recoverable publication. owner.acquire returns `actor_file`/`actor_id`/`lease_epoch` for the owner and `operator_actor_file` for the refreshed operator. Return its path, actor ID and epoch. Concurrent acquires have exactly one winner; an existing owner blocks even when mode differs. owner.release requires the current owner credential; increment epoch and revoke owner credentials. Preserve operator recovery authority across every acquire/release/recover by rotating its descriptor and credential through recoverable intent; do not make an old execution credential an operator. owner.recover requires operator authority plus reason and reconciliation of the durable active/unreconciled jobs; never timeout alone. AP00018 has no jobs and requires both durable jobs and reconciled_job_ids empty. Increment epoch, revoke prior execution actors and clear owner; acquiring again is explicit. Return current operator credential path/epoch where rotation is required. Lost acknowledgements at every credential publication boundary must leave either the old consistent pair or a recoverable intent; never a committed receipt pointing at missing credential bytes. Recovery retries reconcile intent before new work. Failure to reconcile returns recovery_required without accepting another owner. Intent records contain paths/digests/IDs, never plaintext secrets; staged credential bytes remain private 0600. Use one fixed private `credential-intent.json` and private staged/rollback files under actors. Before changing final credentials, stage+fsync all new bytes and rollback copies, then persist+directory-fsync intent containing the canonical request digest, old revision/state digest, candidate state, response/receipt and old/new credential descriptors/paths/digests. Candidate state contains no secrets. Publish final credential files with fsync/replace/directory-fsync, then publish state+receipt through StateStore, then remove intent and private stages with directory fsync. Bootstrap uses the state sidecar lock without recursively locking; factor a locked initialization entry internally. Never acquire a second flock for the same operation. A crash before durable intent leaves only unreferenced private stages; it changes no final credential or state. A crash after intent is reconciled forward exactly once from validated old/candidate state and verified staged/final hashes, or returns recovery_required retaining evidence. A successful receipt is never emitted until final files match its descriptors. Reconciliation admission: strict envelope and project/workflow binding validation precede reconciliation; only the identical intent request authenticated by its recorded old/new authorizing descriptor (or the identical null-bootstrap request) may finish it. All unrelated/invalid requests return recovery_required/wrong_binding without changing bytes. Snapshot never reconciles; it reports recovery_required while an intent exists. A changed bootstrap request ID cannot reconcile another bootstrap. Frozen fixtures enumerate crashes at stage, intent, each credential publication, state publication and cleanup; after recovery the original caller can retrieve the exact receipt using its historical credential. Rejection byte preservation is measured after admitted intent reconciliation only for that successful matching recovery request; rejected calls never reconcile.

### Export and installed evidence

`contracts/controller/workflow-v1.json` is canonical JSON Schema for durable state and protocol/payload/response definitions. `fixtures-v1.json` freezes named positive/negative scenarios with explicit expected errors and no real secrets. `provenance.json` records OVCAQ repository, exact pin, source-to-target symbol and test maps, hashes, preserved invariants and deliberate exclusions/divergences; preserve MIT attribution in extracted files. Exporter computes SHA-256 of raw schema/fixture bytes and produces `contracts/controller-v1.json`, strict JSON with exactly `{protocol_major, package_version, schema_digest, fixture_digest, operations, capabilities}`. protocol_major is integer 1; package_version equals plugin manifest version; digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex; operations/capabilities are unique string lists containing only implemented items. No symlink path components, regular file, under 16777216 bytes. Runtime contract reads installed assets and matches digests/identities; package version may add `+<build>` only. Export is deterministic and cannot read live workflow state. README documents raw bundle SHA-256 and the single installed argv above. No package version bump/publication or installation is authorized.

## Data flow

CLI parses bounded input → resolves explicit project → acquires store lock → validates contract/binding/auth and intent admission → reconciles only an admitted matching intent → checks receipt then current epoch/revision → validates operation → durably prepares intent/staged credentials → publishes credentials and receipt/state → emits bounded redacted response. Bootstrap shares the same lock with concurrent bootstrap calls. Later operation handlers never bypass the store transaction. Contract export is read-only except its explicit output bundle.

## Reuse inventory

- OVCAQ pinned `src/ovcaq/state/store.py`: extract StateStore durability implementation and exceptions, replacing only schema imports and temporary-prefix branding where recorded. No simplified second writer.
- OVCAQ pinned `src/ovcaq/state/schema.py`: reuse strict bounded JSON and owned-field validation patterns; separate workflow fields and explicit new controller identity/lease/receipt schema. Do not import OVCAQ.
- OVCAQ pinned `src/ovcaq/paths.py`: reuse root/path containment concepts. `state/paths.py` arbitrary mutation is intentionally excluded.
- `tools/autopilot/export-policy.py` and existing contract tests: reuse raw-byte digest/version and installed relocation testing patterns; production imports remain within the plugin root.
- No existing actor/lease/receipt controller implementation found. Searches cover read/load/decode, validate/check/verify, create/init, resolve/lookup and store/state/actor/lease/receipt; existing facade/contracts are known-term controls. Research evidence records exact commands and findings.

## Alternatives considered

1. Smallest diff: import OVCAQ services directly. Rejected: independently distributable package cannot rely on upper layers or source checkout.
2. Copy the whole OVCAQ state machine. Rejected: process/capability launcher/control ownership would become duplicate authority and expose later families prematurely.
3. Chosen: extract tested transaction mechanics, explicitly characterize workflow schema adaptation, add four kernel operations and credential/receipt fence. More work than imports buys standalone relocation and a versioned producer boundary without a second backend.

## Risks & edge cases

Bob is the operator and owner of recovery. No live state migration occurs: the new private store refuses foreign/unsupported schema rather than converting the current batch. Immutable package rollback, authenticated intent reconciliation and the explicit private archive/new-workflow procedure provide operator recovery; fenced forensic restore is never a way to roll back protocol effects; downgrade refuses newer state. POSIX flock/fsync support is required and unsupported filesystems fail explicitly. Credentials prevent accidental cross-role use, not unrestricted filesystem access. Finite receipt capacity preserves replay semantics at the cost of eventual explicit recovery/migration. Next changes are lifecycle/jobs, review policy and record commits; reserved namespaces and durable job reconciliation support them without granting their capabilities now. Bootstrap and credential rotation are the largest crash-consistency risks and require boundary injection. Snapshot may reveal workflow metadata but never secrets. No deletion/export compliance obligation beyond local operator-owned files is introduced; snapshot exports nonsecret state, deliberate project removal is operator-controlled.

## Test strategy outline

First freeze source ownership, source-to-target/test maps and fixtures; then test store/schema/path equivalence, protocol/receipts, actor/lease fencing and installed export. Required scenarios: kernel_field_ownership, contract_examples, kernel_equivalence, concurrent_cas (real subprocesses), corrupt_state_recovery, lease_exclusion, wrong_actor, epoch_revoked, lost_ack_replay, fresh_open_replay, controller_bundle_reproducible, controller_without_upper_layers, contract_bundle_pinnable, unsupported_operation_refused. Test rejected calls preserve raw state/backup/credential bytes, duplicate/NaN/deep/oversized inputs, symlink/hardlink/FIFO/path escape, concurrent bootstrap, every durability/credential intent boundary and operator recovery after owner revocation. Installed tests copy only the plugin into an isolated root, exclude checkout/OVCAQ/Tower/author-home from imports and environment, and run CLI subprocesses with bounded deadlines. Run PRD's Python 3.12 pytest command and repository validator. Real host execution remains unavailable without separate probe evidence.

# Cardinal sins (immediate blockers)


Flag any of these as blockers regardless of justification. They are non-negotiable because getting them wrong has asymmetric, usually irreversible cost:

- No rollback plan for stateful changes
- Secrets in config files, plaintext environment variables, or source code
- Single point of failure on a write path, without explicit acceptance and justification
- No identified human owner for production operation
- No observability for user-visible operations (no way to know if it is broken)
- "We will figure it out later" attached to a load-bearing concern (security, data integrity, observability, compliance)
- Unbounded resource consumption with no limits, quotas, or backpressure
- Schema changes without a migration plan
- Vendor lock-in for critical infrastructure without an exit strategy
- Authentication or authorization deferred to a later phase
- Data deletion, correction, or export with no defined path (compliance trap)
- Persistent data without a backup and tested restore procedure
- Public API contracts without a versioning strategy
- Hardcoded credentials, keys, or tokens anywhere in the doc or referenced code
- Critical decisions made by acclamation without recorded alternatives or rationale

# Use-Model Dispatch Contract

Canonical shared contract for the four dispatch skills: `use-codex`, `use-gemini`, `use-qwen`, `use-sonnet`. Each skill's SKILL.md keeps only backend-specific content (model/multiplier policy, flag quick-reference, prerequisites) and points here for everything below. When wording here and in a SKILL.md disagree, this file wins.

Every skill dispatches through its helper: `~/.agents/skills/use-<backend>/scripts/<backend>-run.sh` (backend: codex, gemini, qwen, sonnet).

## Prompt Delivery

**IMPORTANT**: Always use `-f` with a temp file for prompts to avoid shell escaping issues.

```bash
# Write prompt to temp file, then run
echo 'Your prompt here (can contain "quotes", parens(), etc.)' > /tmp/model-prompt.txt
~/.agents/skills/use-<backend>/scripts/<backend>-run.sh -f /tmp/model-prompt.txt
```

Prompts pass via argument or `-f` file, never stdin.

## Child Stdin Policy

Every headless child CLI invocation (the `-p`/`--print`/`codex exec` dispatch paths, plus preflight probes and the `mise env` PATH lookup) redirects the child's stdin with `< /dev/null`, so an unattended background dispatch can never hang on a child reading the inherited stdin (the PRD 00040 hang class). Documented exception: interactive (`-i`), bare `-r`/`--resume`, and `-c`/`--continue` invocations keep stdin - they legitimately need the TTY. Never dispatch those modes unattended.

## Error Stream Convention

Usage and preflight errors (missing prompt, missing prompt file, backend CLI not found) print to stderr and exit non-zero. stdout is reserved for model output and the tee'd `-o` run log.

## Background Dispatch and Waiting

A run-script call can run for many minutes. When you need to do other work while it runs, or you are inside an autopilot run:

1. Dispatch the helper script with `run_in_background: true`. The dispatch tool result returns the task's output file path.
2. Wait with the `TaskOutput` tool: `TaskOutput(task_id, block=true, timeout=600000)` (600000 ms = 10 min is the max per call). It returns when the task completes or at the deadline. It is the watchdog.
3. On completion, `Read` the output file. On a timeout return, treat it as an infrastructure hang (see Error Handling); do not silently re-dispatch.

**Never hand-roll a polling loop.** Do not pass a `while`/`if`/`wc -c` stability loop to `Monitor` or `Bash` to detect completion. Such commands contain shell control flow that Warden cannot statically analyze, so they prompt for approval, which stalls an unattended autopilot run. The harness already notifies you when a background task finishes; `TaskOutput` is the only wait primitive you need.

## Following Up

- Attended sessions: after every run-script command, use `AskUserQuestion` to confirm next steps.
- Unattended sessions (`CLAUDE_UNATTENDED=1`): never call `AskUserQuestion`; take the documented default, log it as `defaulted:<decision>` in the run report, and follow `<autopilot-plugin-root>/skills/run-autopilot/references/unattended-contract.md`.
- By default each run is independent - a follow-up task is a new run with a new prompt, so restate the relevant context. Where the backend supports resuming, the resumed session carries the original run's model and context over (see each SKILL.md for its resume flags).
- Restate the permission mode when proposing follow-up actions (attended sessions).

## Error Handling

- Stop and report failures whenever a run-script command exits non-zero. Attended: request direction before retrying. Unattended (`CLAUDE_UNATTENDED=1`): retry at most 2 times, then mark the step FAILED with the captured stderr, per the unattended contract cited above.
- Before using high-impact permission flags (`-y`/`--yolo` and backend equivalents) ask user permission via AskUserQuestion unless already given; unattended, use them only where the calling skill's documented defaults already grant them.
- When output includes warnings or partial results, summarize them and ask how to adjust (attended) or log them in the run report and proceed (unattended).

### Error taxonomy

A non-zero exit is not one failure — recognize the class and act per its row before retrying (the retry bounds above still apply: attended asks, unattended retries ≤2 then FAILED). Each row names an observable recognition signal and an observable outcome; a caller that hits this case answers "what do I do when the CLI fails this way" from the table, not from memory.

| Class | Recognize by | Action |
|-------|--------------|--------|
| **Auth expired** | stderr names auth/login/credentials/token — `not logged in`, `authentication failed`, `401`, `re-authenticate` | Do NOT retry blindly (a retry re-fails identically). Mark the step **FAILED** and print the re-auth hint (the backend's login command — e.g. `codex login`, `gemini`/`copilot` auth). Unattended cannot re-auth, so it stops here rather than burning retries. |
| **Quota / rate exhausted** | stderr names quota/rate/usage — `monthly quota exceeded`, `rate limit`, `429`, `usage limit`. DISTINCT from auth: the credential is valid, the budget is spent | Mark **FAILED** — retrying spends nothing and fixes nothing. When the CLI reports a reset time, **quote it in the run report** so the caller knows when a retry could succeed. (A Carl/copilot `monthly quota exceeded` is this class — a runtime skip, not a prerequisite failure.) |
| **CLI died mid-run** | non-zero exit with a truncated/partial `-o` file (crash, OOM-kill, SIGKILL) | **Salvage** what landed in the `-o` file, mark it **PARTIAL** in the run report, and treat the run as FAILED-with-partial — never present a truncated result as the full answer. |
| **Empty output despite rc 0** | helper exited 0 but the `-o` file is empty (0 bytes) or whitespace-only | Treat as **FAILED**, not success (a silent empty result reads as a passed review that never happened). **Quote the run's stderr** in the report — the real cause is usually there. |

**Codex exit-4 salvage (`codex_review_run.py` callers only).** Exit 4 and the `codex-review-last.jsonl` sidecar are produced by `run-autopilot/scripts/codex_review_run.py`, **not** by `codex-run.sh` — that helper returns codex's real exit code and writes no sidecar. So this row applies to callers dispatching through `codex_review_run.py` (the review path); a caller using `codex-run.sh` directly never sees exit 4 and has nothing to salvage. Exit 4 means codex ran but the wrapper flagged failure (e.g. quota), and it has a documented FALSE-POSITIVE mode: the quota/error markers can match codex's own command-line args or gateguard ERROR noise while codex actually finished, and the `-o` file may be unwritten even though the work completed. Before treating exit 4 as the Quota class above, check the sidecar (its last-run JSONL): if it holds a COMPLETE result (the expected findings/verdict content), **salvage it and treat the run as succeeded**. Only when nothing salvageable is in the sidecar → FAILED. `review-work-completion` carries the review-specific `D{n}:`-verdict variant (the doubt lens Bob runs). Memory: `project_codex_review_run_exit4_false_positive`.

### Implementor-mode divergence (codex, PRD 00105)

Everything above describes codex in its **reviewer/analysis** role, where a run
produces text and the caller reads it. PRD 00105 added codex as an
**implementor** rung (`work/SKILL.md` step 3; fences and arms in
`run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md` § Codex rung), where a run edits the
work-tree and a test gate judges it. That path deliberately departs from three
rules above. This file wins on disagreement, so the departures are recorded
here rather than asserted only at the call site:

| Rule above | Implementor path | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "Stop and report failures whenever a run-script command exits non-zero" | Exit code never decides the outcome. Completion is judged by the `-o` file plus the step-5.5 test gate. | Exit-code trust is exactly what the exit-4 false positive punished. A codex run that edited the tree correctly but exited non-zero has still done the work, and the gate can see that; the exit code cannot. |
| "Unattended: retry at most 2 times, then mark the step FAILED" | No retry at this rung. An infra failure falls back to Claude at the task's tier immediately, with no `escalation_reason` stamp. | The ladder, not the contract, owns implementor budgets (`model-ladder.md` § Per-rung budgets: 2 dispatches, initial + one feedback retry, never a repair). A contract-level retry would stack on top of the ladder's budget and double-spend it. |
| "Before using high-impact permission flags (`-y`/`--yolo` and backend equivalents) ask user permission … unattended, use them only where the calling skill's documented defaults already grant them" | Dispatches with `-a` (edit-enabled sandbox) unattended. | This IS the calling-skill grant the rule points at: `work/references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex dispatch documents `-a` as the rung's default, and `model-ladder.md` § Codex rung records that it runs under a strictly weaker `Bash`-hook set than any Claude rung, with `_WORK_CODEX_RUNG=off` as the revert. The grant is narrow — it covers the implementor rung only, never a reviewer dispatch. |

An implementor run also has a failure mode no reviewer run has: the helper
exits 0 with non-empty output but changes **nothing**, because this host's
PreToolUse hooks denied the edits and codex explained the denial in prose. That
is classified infra, not capability — see `model-ladder.md` § Codex rung arm 2.
